proposed_updates.emetogenic_risk: Minimal per NCCP 00102 v6; do not replace with the combination classification
proposed_updates.supportive_care: This is a minimal-emetic-risk oral regimen in the NCCP plan. Anti-sickness medicine is chosen to match symptoms and interactions; do not add over-the-counter medicines without checking. Agree a hydration and diarrhoea plan, and report inability to drink or persistent symptoms.
proposed_updates.schedule: Vemurafenib twice daily, about 12 hours apart, every day. A 28-day review cycle does not mean a planned tablet-free week.
proposed_updates.administration: The usual starting dose is 960 mg twice daily, about 12 hours apart; the prescribed dose may differ after review. Swallow tablets whole with water. Vemurafenib can be taken with or without food, but do not regularly take both daily doses on an empty stomach. Keep a consistent routine and follow the pharmacy label.
proposed_updates.monitoring: Blood count, kidney and liver tests before each cycle. NCCP specifies ECG every four weeks for the first 12 weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose changes. Its skin-review row states week eight then every 12 weeks; current Zelboraf product information instead requires monthly prescriber skin examinations. The team should supply a reconciled written skin-check plan using the current product information.
proposed_updates.phase_boundaries: This is vemurafenib monotherapy. It is not the cobimetinib combination and has no cobimetinib seven-day break. The team must plan any radiotherapy because BRAF treatment can increase radiation-related reactions.

proposed_updates.emetogenic_risk: Minimal to low per NCCP 00237 v6; local policy
proposed_updates.supportive_care: NCCP classifies dabrafenib as minimal-to-low emetogenic risk; anti-sickness treatment follows local and individual need. Agree a written fever plan and keep a thermometer and actual urgent-contact number. The team may prescribe fever treatment and hydration advice after assessment; fever medicine is not a substitute for contacting them. Anti-sickness treatment is selected individually.
proposed_updates.schedule: Dabrafenib twice daily, about 12 hours apart, every day. Take it on an empty stomach; there is no planned tablet-free week.
proposed_updates.administration: The usual starting dose is 150 mg twice daily, about 12 hours apart. Take capsules at least one hour before or at least two hours after food. Swallow whole with water. Use the prescribed strength and dose, and check the label again after any interruption or dose change.
proposed_updates.monitoring: Monthly blood count, kidney and liver tests, and monthly skin review. Repeat ECG when clinically indicated. NCCP also describes head-and-neck review every three months and other surveillance according to the individual assessment; this is separate from the cancer-response scan plan.
proposed_updates.phase_boundaries: This is dabrafenib monotherapy for advanced melanoma. Do not import the food, heart-testing, fertility or duration instructions of a different BRAF/MEK combination. The NCCP fever table states 38.5°C, while current EMA product information states interruption at 38°C for monotherapy; this guide uses the earlier current-product safety trigger and the team must reconcile the written plan.

proposed_updates.emetogenic_risk: Cobimetinib minimal to low; vemurafenib minimal to low in NCCP 00373 v3; local policy
proposed_updates.supportive_care: NCCP lists each component as minimal-to-low emetogenic risk; follow local and individual anti-sickness policy. Agree a diarrhoea, fluid-intake and nausea plan; contact the team if symptoms persist or you cannot drink. Check all prescribed, over-the-counter and herbal medicines for interactions before taking them. The seven-day cobimetinib break is planned; extra breaks or restarting doses require the team’s instructions.
proposed_updates.schedule: Every 28 days: cobimetinib once daily on days 1–21, then seven days off; vemurafenib twice daily continues on all 28 days unless held by the team.
proposed_updates.administration: Usual starting doses are cobimetinib 60 mg once daily on days 1–21 and vemurafenib 960 mg twice daily, about 12 hours apart, continuously. Cobimetinib can be taken with or without food. Avoid regularly taking both daily vemurafenib doses on an empty stomach. Swallow both medicines whole and follow the separate labels.
proposed_updates.monitoring: Blood count, kidney/liver tests and LDH before each cycle. Current Cotellic product information adds CPK and creatinine monthly, and LVEF after the first month then at least every three months until treatment stops. ECG is every four weeks for the first 12 weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose changes. Arrange monthly skin checks under current vemurafenib product information. New visual symptoms need prompt eye assessment; symptoms can require extra tests between scheduled checks.
proposed_updates.phase_boundaries: Only cobimetinib has the planned days 22–28 break. Vemurafenib continues. ECG measures rhythm; an echocardiogram or other LVEF test measures pumping function, and one does not replace the other. Radiation treatment needs a separate coordinated plan.

proposed_updates.supportive_care: NCCP classifies ipilimumab as low emetogenic risk; anti-sickness treatment is individual. Routine infusion premedication is not usually required, but previous reactions may change the plan. Do not start steroids or alter prescribed steroid tapers or hormone replacement without the team.
proposed_updates.schedule: Ipilimumab by IV infusion once every 21 days, up to four doses. Complete within 16 weeks of the first dose, whichever limit comes first.
proposed_updates.administration: The source dose is ipilimumab 3 mg/kg over 90 minutes on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, with observation for one hour after the infusion. Allow additional time for symptom review, blood results and preparation. Report any previous infusion reaction before treatment.
proposed_updates.monitoring: Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests before every cycle, plus a careful symptom review. Cortisol and other tests are added when symptoms suggest endocrine or other immune effects. Normal routine blood results do not exclude colitis, lung, nerve or other inflammation.
proposed_updates.phase_boundaries: This guide describes ipilimumab monotherapy at 3 mg/kg. It is not the nivolumab combination and does not automatically lead to nivolumab maintenance. A four-dose treatment course does not mean immune risks end after dose four.

proposed_updates.supportive_care: Avelumab has minimal emetogenic risk in current NCCP. Premedication for the first four infusions prevents or reduces infusion reactions and is distinct from anti-sickness treatment. Confirm the medicine names and timing on the appointment plan. Other symptom treatments depend on the individual; immune-related symptoms need assessment rather than self-treatment alone.
proposed_updates.schedule: Avelumab by IV infusion every 14 days, continuing while beneficial and tolerable. The first four infusions have a specific premedication plan; four is not the course limit.
proposed_updates.administration: Avelumab 800 mg is infused over 60 minutes. An antihistamine and paracetamol are given before the first four infusions; NCCP specifies at least 30 minutes beforehand. After that, premedication is at consultant discretion if no reaction occurred. Allow additional time for checks, preparation and observation.
proposed_updates.monitoring: Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests before every cycle. The nurse watches for infusion reactions and the team checks for bowel, breathing, skin, endocrine and other immune symptoms. Additional tests depend on symptoms, not just the routine blood panel.
proposed_updates.phase_boundaries: This is the Merkel-cell cancer context after chemotherapy under current NCCP. It is not avelumab maintenance for urothelial cancer. Evidence from untreated first-line Merkel-cell cohorts must not be presented as the evidence for this specific post-chemotherapy indication.

proposed_updates.emetogenic_risk: Low combination induction; minimal nivolumab maintenance per NCCP 00551 v7a
proposed_updates.supportive_care: NCCP classifies the combination phase as low emetogenic risk and nivolumab alone as minimal risk. Anti-sickness treatment is individual. Routine infusion premedication is not usually required; a previous reaction may alter that plan. Steroid or hormone treatment for immune effects must have a written follow-up plan.
proposed_updates.schedule: Up to four combination infusions, 21 days apart, then nivolumab alone every two or four weeks as prescribed; four stamps record combination doses only.
proposed_updates.administration: During combination treatment, nivolumab 3 mg/kg is infused first over 30 minutes, then ipilimumab 1 mg/kg over 30 minutes. Maintenance may be nivolumab IV 240 mg every two weeks or IV 480 mg every four weeks, or the prescribed subcutaneous alternative of 600 mg every two weeks or 1200 mg every four weeks. In this melanoma source, IV 240 mg takes 30 minutes and IV 480 mg takes 60 minutes; subcutaneous administration takes about three to five minutes.
proposed_updates.monitoring: Blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests before every cycle, with symptom review during combination and maintenance phases. Cortisol and other organ tests are added when indicated. Recheck route, dose, interval and the maintenance start date when phases change.
proposed_updates.phase_boundaries: NCCP identifies nivolumab 3 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg for melanoma as an unlicensed dosing posology in Ireland, despite reimbursement. Your clinician should explain this, the available alternatives and uncertainties, document informed consent under hospital policy, and follow the hospital Drug and Therapeutics Committee or equivalent acknowledgement process. CheckMate 511 primarily compared safety; it did not prove that this schedule has equal survival benefit to nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg.

proposed_updates.emetogenic_risk: High per NCCP 00464 v3; preventive antiemetic regimen required under local policy
proposed_updates.supportive_care: Dacarbazine has high nausea-and-vomiting risk, so a planned preventive anti-sickness regimen is needed under the local protocol, including clear take-home instructions. The NCCP line that routine premedication is usually unnecessary does not remove this antiemetic requirement. Ask what to take regularly, what is rescue treatment and when to call if it fails.
proposed_updates.schedule: Dacarbazine by IV infusion on day 1, repeated every 21 days for up to six cycles, or stopped earlier for progression or unacceptable toxicity.
proposed_updates.administration: The NCCP dose is dacarbazine 850 mg/m² on day 1 in one litre of saline over one hour, with the infusion protected from light. The individual dose is prescribed using body size and clinical review. Allow extra time for blood results, anti-sickness medicine, preparation and any other fluids. Tell the nurse immediately about pain, burning, swelling or redness around the infusion.
proposed_updates.monitoring: Full blood count, kidney and liver function before every cycle. Blood-count suppression can be delayed: the product information describes the lowest counts often three to four weeks after a dose, so a 21-day appointment does not guarantee recovery. Extra blood tests are arranged when clinically needed.
proposed_updates.phase_boundaries: This is single-agent dacarbazine at the NCCP 850 mg/m² dose. It is not an immune-checkpoint or BRAF-targeted regimen. Historical studies often used 1000 mg/m² and different treatment settings; their response or survival figures are not a precise forecast for this 850 mg/m² course.
